newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Activist seeks role in Timorese Spanish mission.
newsitem.headline: Activist seeks role in Timorese Spanish mission.

text.p: An Indonesian human rights activist said on Wednesday he hoped to soon meet five East Timorese who had taken refuge in the Spanish embassy in Jakarta to discuss a possible end to the week-long drama.

Johannes Princen, director of the Institute for the Defence of Human Rights, said he hoped to meet with embassy and International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) officials at the mission on Wednesday to receive permission to speak with the five Timorese.
Deputy mission head, Alicia Moral, told Reuters on Wednesday the five, who entered on September 10, were still in the embassy in Central Jakarta. She refused to give any more details.
Princen said he hoped to discuss with the Timorese the possibility of either arranging guarantees of safety from local security authorities for them to leave the embassy or asylum in Portugal.
"I am not allowed yet to talk to them by instruction by the Spanish government to the ambassador," Princen said, adding that he had to meet with the ICRC to seek help in arranging a visit.
"The thing is that, if possible, they do not want to go to Portugal," Princen, who said he had unspecified contact with the Timorese, told Reuters.
East Timorese sources said the intentions of the five are not clear.

Princen, a Dutch-born Indonesian national, has in the past acted as a mediator in similar embassy break-ins in the Russian, Dutch and Australian embassies which have resulted in the Timorese leaving the missions without leaving the country.

The former Portuguese colony of East Timor was invaded by Indonesia in 1975 and annexed the following year in an act not recognised by the United Nations. The U.N. still regards Portugal as the adminstering power.
Since September last year, a total of 84 East Timorese have been granted asylum in Portugal after entering foreign embassies in Jakarta. All have had their travel facilitated by the ICRC.
